newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARIAN SHARES SEEN UP, PROFIT-TAKING POSSIBLE.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARIAN SHARES SEEN UP, PROFIT-TAKING POSSIBLE.

text.p: A rally in Hungarian share prices is expected to slow down on Thursday, but the BUX index is seen remaining in positive territory, traders said. But they said recent gains could justify profit-taking.

"The rise could easily continue, but I think that the bulk of investors is already contemplating as to whether unload papers or keep on buying," said Peter Tolgyesi of Buda-Cash Brokerhaz. "The story is already not about fundamentals but a euphory."
Andrea Keresztesi of ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett also said some investors were considering to sell off their holdings and the market could consolidate recent gains.
"Mainly small investors might sell, while funds would not do so because they cannot buy anything instead," she said.
She added that shares such as tile maker Zalakeramia which fell in the past few days, might grab increasing attention.

However, traders added they have seen no signs yet of any substantial retreat, as the market is backed by earnings hopes mainly by leading companies oil firm MOL and OTP Bank, a strong dollar, and positive sentiment on foreign markets.
On Wednesday the BUX index finished at a third successive closing high of 8,483.79 points, up 315.66 points or 3.86 percent.
